audit.whatIsWrong: Level 3, First item and 2+ items were given to Gnar while their own whys say the opposite: whys[2] ends '— even', whys[5] says 'keeps the lane even', and whys[6] says 'Lucian out-scales the duel'.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Lucian on 1431 games at 51.64% — a knife-edge lane whose one clear Gnar row is level 2 and whose one clear Lucian row is two items. The prose already said exactly that.
audit.corrected: Level 3 and First item flipped to Skill; 2+ items flipped to Lucian at 3/10 with phases[6].why rewritten. Level 2 left with Gnar — the Hyper window is real and the packet agrees.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire page is built on 'engage when Relentless Pursuit is down' with no cooldown and no mention that it refunds.
audit.why: Relentless Pursuit is 16/15.5/15/14.5/14, but Lightslinger attacks reduce its cooldown — so every double-shot he lands on a minion or on you pulls the dash back sooner. 'Wait for his E to be down' is therefore a moving target, and a Gnar who commits on a stale count gets punished. It also costs 0 mana at rank 5.
audit.corrected: The 14-16s figure and the Lightslinger refund written into mid and whys[5].
sources: enemyKit E text: 'Lightslinger attacks reduce Relentless Pursuit's cooldown'

audit.whatIsWrong: Lightslinger's immobilize clause is absent from both layers, in a matchup whose whole plan is landing a stun.
audit.why: Riot's Lightslinger text: when a nearby enemy champion is immobilized, Lucian's next 2 basic attacks deal bonus magic damage. Gnar's Wallop and GNAR! both immobilize — so every stun Gnar lands hands Lucian two empowered attacks. That inverts the page's advice: a Wallop thrown for chip actively pays him, and the stun is only correct when it converts to a kill or a disengage. This is the single most important interaction in the matchup and it was on neither layer.
audit.corrected: Written into mid, in the same paragraph that tells the reader to Wallop.
sources: ownerKit W and R hardCC flags

audit.whatIsWrong: Nine content fields are written in first person — 'my squishy Mini body', 'I can kite back', 'I'm stuck in fragile Mini', 'my telegraphed Mega casts'.
audit.why: The rest of the site is second person, and a coaching page that switches to 'I' reads as somebody else's diary rather than instructions to the reader.
audit.corrected: whys[2], whys[3], whys[4], whys[6], early, mid and late converted to second person at equal length.

audit.why: The packet flagged 'Save Relentless Pursuit' in wants.foe[1] as a probable wrong name. False positive — the flagged span includes the leading verb; Relentless Pursuit is the correct E name.

edits.before: This is all about Rage timing. If Mega lines up I can bait his E dash, transform, and Wallop-stun him for a real trade — or shove him into the wall with GNAR! for a kill. If I'm stuck in Mini with Rage on cooldown when he commits an E onto me, I'm a fragile ranged target with no escape and he wins that exchange. At 6 I get no new spell, so my power there is purely whether Mega is available; he gets The Culling (R) but in lane it's just extra poke — manage the bar around his all-in windows.
edits.after: This is all about Rage timing. If Mega lines up you can bait his E dash, transform, and Wallop-stun him for a real trade — or shove him into a wall with GNAR! for a kill. Know the price first: Lightslinger empowers his next two attacks whenever a nearby enemy is immobilized, so your own stun feeds his burst — spend it to kill, never to chip. His attacks also refund Relentless Pursuit off its 14-16s, so a spent dash returns early. At 6 you gain no new spell; your power is purely whether Mega is up.

edits.before: Even lane, but Lucian pulls ahead once he hits two items — his DPS and E-dash spacing kite my Mini form and let him slip every telegraphed Wallop and GNAR! cast. My value shifts off the 1v1 and onto teamfights, where a wall-ult on him or his backline is one of the best engages in the game. Don't try to solo-duel a fed Lucian in a side lane late; group and let GNAR! do the work.

notes: The find worth acting on beyond the chart: Lightslinger grants Lucian two empowered attacks whenever a nearby enemy champion is immobilized. Gnar's Wallop and GNAR! both immobilize, so the page's core instruction — land the stun — has a cost it never disclosed. Also, the full layer's whole tracking frame ('engage on Relentless Pursuit's cooldown', repeated in focus.text, loading, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and four report rows) is shakier than it looks, because Lightslinger attacks refund that cooldown continuously. I corrected the content layer; the full-layer boilerplate still states it flatly.
